title: Henri IV to Andre Hurault de Maisse, ambassador at Venice, 3 November 1592 - 27 April 1593 (BnF fr. 16093 ff. 370, 373, 406, 410)

steps.what: Tomokiyo's Henri IV page re-read as HTML rather than as the text dump in gallica_sweep/src: the four leaves fall in two different cipher sections, each with siblings in the same volume, so the entry's class B and 'no sibling found' were both wrong.
fr. 16093 resolved to ark btv1b90074656 by Gallica SRU and the folio-to-canvas offsets calibrated by reading folio numbers off the leaves.
The opening of f. 370 transcribed group by group (80 groups) from the native-resolution scan.

Blind frequency analysis of the transcription: 94% of groups in a contiguous band 1-22, commonest value 14.5%, sparse values above the band - a simple substitution with a small nomenclator, not the assumed homophonic system.

Blind known-plaintext alignment of the transcription against the Brienne clear text placed 12 groups against a shuffled-cipher control of mean 8.2 and p95 11 - at the noise floor, because the transcription mis-split 9 7 as 97 and homophony was wrongly assumed.

The old Harlay piece numbers on each leaf (224, 226, 247, 251) matched to Berger de Xivrey's citations, which give a clear copy in fonds Brienne 13 = NAF 6984 for each; the four copies located on the images by heading and preamble.
Tomokiyo's two key images fetched from his page (invisible in a text dump) and cipher 1 transcribed to key1.tsv.
The key applied to the 80 transcribed groups of f. 370 and the result normalised against Brienne 13 fol. 102v: 81 of 81 characters identical.
All four letters read from the Brienne clear copies; f. 406 shown to be the duplicate of f. 404, so the four leaves are three despatches.

Novelty re-examined after Lasry's note on 'undeciphered'. G. Lasry (21 Sept 2026): on cryptiana 'undeciphered' means no interlinear or nearby deciphered copy, not unsolved; unsolved material is on the unsolved page. The page no longer says Tomokiyo 'never applied' his keys; the claim is a published reading only.

outcome.method_basis: The content of all four letters comes from contemporary clear copies in fonds Brienne 13 (BnF NAF 6984), located through the Harlay piece numbers and Berger de Xivrey; Tomokiyo's published key for 'Maisse's Cipher (1592)' was applied only to the 81 transcribed characters of f. 370, which match the Brienne copy.
outcome.notes: The content of all four letters is settled by the contemporary clear copies. Group-by-group decipherment covers only the transcribed opening of f. 370, verified letter-for-letter; ff. 373, 406 and 410 are not transcribed, and cipher 2 was not applied.

prior.where: A key for each of the two ciphers published by Tomokiyo as images on cryptiana, reconstructed from sibling leaves and no reading of these four published; he lists them as undeciphered (no contemporary decipherment, not unsolved), so he may have read them; contemporary clear copies of all four letters in Brienne 13 (NAF 6984), unprinted; Berger de Xivrey prints a sibling (t. III p. 719)
